reason: E2 supports the general importance of scale adhesion and Cr₂O₃ formation for oxidation resistance, but none of the cited evidence addresses the specific Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy, the competitive Cr/Ti oxidation mechanism, the proposed reducing-environment behavior, or the direct link between scale quality and mechanical degradation.
premises: Cr and Ti in the alloy undergo competitive oxidation, forming mixed Cr₂O₃/TiO₂ scales.
Under oxidizing conditions, this mixed scale is loosely adherent, spalls, and initiates microcracking.
Under reducing conditions, limited oxidation causes elemental segregation and interfacial embrittlement.
The quality (adhesion, continuity) of the oxide scale directly governs mechanical degradation.
